chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) over the deceased, and he said: 'Five Takbirat. When you say Takbir, say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Then say: O Allah, this one lying before us is Your servant and the son of Your servant, and You have taken his soul to Yourself, and he has come into need of Your mercy, while You are independent of his punishment. O Allah, we do not know from his outward appearance except good, and You are more knowing of his inner self. O Allah, if he was a doer of good, multiply his good, and if he was a doer of evil, overlook his evil. Then you say the second Takbir, then do that in every Takbir.'

My father, Al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the Salat (prayer) over the deceased, and he said: 'As for the believer, it is five Takbirat, and as for the hypocrite, it is four, and there is no Salam (greeting of peace) in it.'

key_terms.اَلتَّكْبِيرِ: Saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), a key component of the funeral prayer
key_terms.اَلصَّلاَةِ: Prayer, specifically the ritual funeral prayer in this context
key_terms.اَلْمُنَافِقُ: The hypocrite, distinguished here by having fewer Takbirat and no Salam
key_terms.سَرِيرَتِهِ: His inner self or hidden state

ai.seo_question: What are the specific recitations and number of Takbirat for praying over a deceased Muslim according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the five-Takbir structure for the believer’s funeral prayer, embedding a concise theological formula that balances hope in divine mercy with the reality of human imperfection. It further clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the believer and the hypocrite (*munafiq*), where the latter receives only four Takbirat without the concluding Salam, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of prayer based on the deceased's spiritual state.
